name: Constellation Energy Corporation
monetization: Sells firm carbon-free nuclear power to hyperscalers under 15–20-year PPAs — Microsoft (Crane/TMI restart), Meta (Clinton) — on top of the largest US nuclear fleet, expanded by Calpine's gas fleet.
description_md: Constellation operates the largest nuclear fleet in the United States (~22GW across roughly two dozen reactors) and, after closing its acquisition of Calpine in 2026, a combined generation fleet of roughly 55GW spanning nuclear, natural gas, and geothermal. It has become the flagship counterparty for hyperscaler nuclear power deals: the September 2024 agreement with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 as the 835MW Crane Clean Energy Center, and the June 2025 20-year agreement with Meta for 1,121MW from the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois.
ai_monetization_md: AI monetization runs through long-dated, investment-grade PPAs that convert merchant nuclear output into contracted revenue at a premium: Microsoft's 20-year PPA funds the first-ever restart of a retired US reactor (Crane, online expected 2027–28), Meta's 20-year Clinton deal replaces an expiring state subsidy with corporate demand, and in Q2 2026 alone Constellation signed a further 920MW of 15–20-year nuclear PPAs (including 176MW with Walmart) starting 2029–2032. Roughly 30% of its clean baseload output is now under long-term contract. PPA prices are undisclosed — only Talen's Amazon deal has a public price — so realized economics are inferred, not known.
ai_strategy_md: Convert the merchant nuclear fleet, plant by plant, into a contracted infrastructure business serving data-center demand: restart retired capacity (Crane), pursue uprates (~1GW+ potential across the fleet, e.g. the Dresden expansion enabled by the Walmart PPA), extend licenses, and use Calpine's dispatchable gas fleet to firm supply and follow load. Management frames the strategy as selling reliability and carbon attributes to the handful of buyers — hyperscalers — willing to sign 20-year paper.
risk_notes_md: PPA prices are undisclosed, so the market is pricing a premium it cannot verify. The Crane restart carries first-of-its-kind execution and NRC risk. Hyperscaler concentration cuts both ways: a pullback in AI power procurement would strand uprate/restart plans premised on it. Political/regulatory risk around co-located and data-center-serving nuclear (FERC interconnection disputes, state ratepayer-protection debates) remains live. Calpine adds commodity gas exposure to a formerly nuclear-heavy story.

events.title: Signs 20-year PPA with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 as Crane Clean Energy Center
events.why_it_matters: The deal that opened the nuclear-for-AI era: a hyperscaler PPA strong enough to bring an entire retired reactor (835MW) back to the grid; price undisclosed.

events.title: Meta signs 20-year, 1,121MW PPA for the Clinton Clean Energy Center
events.why_it_matters: Replaces expiring state subsidy with hyperscaler demand — a template for corporate money substituting for public support in keeping nuclear plants alive.

events.title: Q2 2026: +920MW of new nuclear PPAs; FY2026 EPS guidance raised to $11.50–12.50
events.why_it_matters: Shows nuclear PPA demand broadening beyond the big-three hyperscalers (e.g. Walmart) and the fleet steadily converting from merchant to contracted.
